title: Al mercato
summary: Market and supermarket quantities — un etto, un chilo, una fetta — and paying.

blocks.title: Etto, chilo, fetta
blocks.body: At an Italian market or deli counter, quantities come in specific units: **un etto** (100 grams — the classic deli unit for cured meats and cheese), **un chilo** (1 kilogram), **una fetta** (a slice), and **un pacco** (a pack/package). You can lead with the request yourself: **'Mi dà un etto di prosciutto, per favore.'**
blocks.callout: *Un etto* is doing a lot of work here — ask for *cento grammi* and you'll get a smile, but *un etto* is what people actually say.

blocks.title: Le quantità
blocks.body: Match the unit to what you're buying — weight for deli and produce, pieces for baked goods.

blocks.prompt: How many grams are in *un etto*?
blocks.explain: *Un etto* = 100 grams — the everyday unit at the deli counter, smaller than *un chilo*.

pairs.left: *Mi dà…?* — market/deli counter: 'would you give me…'
pairs.note: Both are polite. *Mi dà* feels especially natural pointing at something on a stall.

blocks.prompt: Type 'I would like a kilo of apples.'
blocks.explain: *Vorrei un chilo di mele.* — quantity + di + the thing.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.
